walkthrough: We want to find the number of different arrangements of the 10 letters of SHOPKEEPER in which all 3 Es are together.

Step 1: Determine letter counts in SHOPKEEPER:
S: 1, H: 1, O: 1, P: 2, K: 1, E: 3, R: 1
Total number of letters is 10.

Step 2: Apply the block method for the grouped Es.
Treat all 3 identical Es as a single combined unit: $(EEE)$.
The items to arrange are now:
$$(EEE), \; \text{S}, \; \text{H}, \; \text{O}, \; \text{P}, \; \text{P}, \; \text{K}, \; \text{R}$$
This gives $1 + 7 = 8$ items.

Step 3: Account for identical items.
Among these 8 items, the letter P appears 2 times, while the unit $(EEE)$ contains identical letters with only 1 internal arrangement ($3!/3! = 1$).

Step 4: Compute the permutations:
$$\text{Arrangements} = \frac{8!}{2!} = \frac{40\,320}{2} = 20\,160$$

hints: Use the subtraction method: total arrangements minus arrangements where the two Ps are together.
Find total arrangements of SHOPKEEPER (10 letters with 2 Ps and 3 Es): $\dfrac{10!}{2! \, 3!} = 302\,400$.
Find arrangements where the two Ps are together by bundling them as $(PP)$ among 9 items with 3 Es: $\dfrac{9!}{3!} = 60\,480$.
walkthrough: We want to find the number of different arrangements of SHOPKEEPER in which the two Ps are not next to each other.
Method 1: Subtraction (complement) method.

Step 1: Calculate total unrestricted arrangements.
SHOPKEEPER has 10 letters: S (1), H (1), O (1), P (2), K (1), E (3), R (1).
$$\text{Total} = \frac{10!}{2! \, 3!} = \frac{3\,628\,800}{2 \times 6} = 302\,400$$

Step 2: Calculate arrangements where the two Ps ARE together.
Treat the two Ps as a block: $(PP)$.
We now arrange 9 items: $(PP)$, S, H, O, K, E, E, E, R, containing 3 identical Es:
$$\text{Ps together} = \frac{9!}{3!} = \frac{362\,880}{6} = 60\,480$$

Step 3: Subtract the forbidden arrangements:
$$\text{Ps not together} = 302\,400 - 60\,480 = 241\,920$$

Method 2: Gap insertion method.
Arrange the 8 letters other than P (S, H, O, K, E, E, E, R):
$$\frac{8!}{3!} = \frac{40\,320}{6} = 6720$$
These 8 letters create $8 + 1 = 9$ available spaces for the Ps.
Choose 2 of the 9 spaces for the two identical Ps:
$$\binom{9}{2} = \frac{9 \times 8}{2} = 36$$
$$\text{Total} = 6720 \times 36 = 241\,920$$
Both methods confirm 241920.

walkthrough: We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen arrangement of the 10 letters of SHOPKEEPER has an E at the beginning and an E at the end.
Method 1: Counting permutations.

Step 1: Total number of arrangements.
From part (b), the total number of unrestricted arrangements is:
$$N = \frac{10!}{2! \, 3!} = 302\,400$$

Step 2: Number of favorable arrangements.
We place an E in position 1 and an E in position 10:
$$E \; \_ \; \_ \; \_ \; \_ \; \_ \; \_ \; \_ \; \_ \; E$$
There are 8 positions remaining, to be filled by the remaining 8 letters:
S (1), H (1), O (1), P (2), K (1), E (1), R (1).
Among these 8 letters, only P is repeated (2 times):
$$\text{Favorable arrangements} = \frac{8!}{2!} = \frac{40\,320}{2} = 20\,160$$

Step 3: Compute the probability:
$$\mathrm{P} = \frac{20\,160}{302\,400} = \frac{2016}{30\,240} = \frac{1}{15} \approx 0.0667$$

Method 2: Direct probability on ends.
Position 1 can be any of the 10 letters, of which 3 are E: $\frac{3}{10}$.
Position 10 can then be any of the remaining 9 letters, of which 2 are E: $\frac{2}{9}$.
$$\text{Probability} = \frac{3}{10} \times \frac{2}{9} = \frac{6}{90} = \frac{1}{15}$$

hints: We are choosing 4 letters from SHOPKEEPER: {S, H, O, P, P, K, E, E, E, R}.
The selection must contain exactly one P, leaving 3 more letters to be chosen from {E, E, E} and the 5 other distinct letters {S, H, O, K, R}.
Split into mutually exclusive cases based on how many Es are chosen: 3 Es, 2 Es, 1 E, or 0 Es.
Calculate combinations from the 5 other letters for each case and sum them: $\binom{5}{0} + \binom{5}{1} + \binom{5}{2} + \binom{5}{3}$.
walkthrough: We are selecting an unordered group of 4 letters from the 10 letters of SHOPKEEPER such that the selection contains exactly one P.

Step 1: Classify the letters available:
- P letters: 2 available (we must choose exactly 1 P).
- E letters: 3 available.
- Other letters: 5 distinct letters {S, H, O, K, R}.

Step 2: Fix 1 P.
Since 1 P is already chosen, we need to choose $4 - 1 = 3$ additional letters from the 3 Es and the 5 other distinct letters {S, H, O, K, R}.

Step 3: Partition into cases based on the number of Es in the selection:

Case 1: 3 Es chosen (Selection: P, E, E, E)
All 3 spots are filled by Es. No other letters are needed:
$$\binom{5}{0} = 1 \text{ selection}$$

Case 2: 2 Es chosen (Selection: P, E, E, _)
Two spots are filled by Es, so 1 letter is chosen from {S, H, O, K, R}:
$$\binom{5}{1} = 5 \text{ selections}$$

Case 3: 1 E chosen (Selection: P, E, _, _)
One spot is filled by an E, so 2 letters are chosen from {S, H, O, K, R}:
$$\binom{5}{2} = \frac{5 \times 4}{2} = 10 \text{ selections}$$

Case 4: 0 Es chosen (Selection: P, _, _, _)
All 3 spots must be chosen from {S, H, O, K, R}:
$$\binom{5}{3} = \frac{5 \times 4 \times 3}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 10 \text{ selections}$$

Step 4: Sum all cases:
$$\text{Total selections} = 1 + 5 + 10 + 10 = 26$$
